summary: Last check before the budget closed: I traced how the transfer marker actually reaches the wire, and it produced one more entry plus a registered discriminator. The trigger is stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case, which performs no check on the sender at all and calls r.hup(campaignTransfer) outright — conspicuous beside its neighbours, since MsgTransferLeader refuses when r.lead == None and MsgReadIndex returns when r.lead == None and otherwise forwards to r.lead, so both consult the follower's own record of the leader while MsgTimeoutNow does not, even though that value sits in the same struct. The chain then runs on legal messages and legal fields: the transfer campaign increments the term and sends MsgVote carrying Context = CampaignTransfer; a receiving voter evaluates force as true and skips the lease; becomeFollower followed by reset clears r.Vote when the term changes and sets r.lead = None, which satisfies canVote, leaving only isUpToDate between the request and a granted vote. So the CheckQuorum lease can be skipped without the MsgForgetLeader classification gap at all — a useful bound on how much protection the lease should be credited with. The judgment follows the same line as the marker itself: both sendTimeoutNow call sites are in stepLeader, so only a leader emits the trigger; a superseded former leader's MsgTimeoutNow carries an older term and is discarded before the follower path is reached; and isUpToDate still applies, so a stale node cannot buy support it would otherwise be refused. Invoking the chain means claiming an authority the sender does not have, which is the byzantine-claim boundary this run already refuted twice, so I recorded it as explained with the defect claim refuted rather than inflating it into a third finding. I registered @timeoutnow_campaign_chain with a concrete discriminator (elect a leader, let its lease go live, deliver a peer-form MsgTimeoutNow to one follower from the third node, and expect the incumbent to grant the vote and step down) and interpreted it in the same update, so nothing is left dangling; two sources were added, including MsgTransferLeader's guard for contrast, and the entry cites the marker entry as the premise it depends on. Final consistency pass: every cited source resolves, every cited receipt exists with all indices in range, problems: none — thirteen questions, thirty-one interpretations, twenty-three knowledge entries, zero gaps and zero uncited executions. No experiment was filed, since no remaining turn could interpret its receipt.
